result:
I'd make people significantly more curious and less tribal.

Most of the world's biggest problems—conflict, bad policy, resistance to progress, even many forms of suffering—aren't primarily caused by lack of resources or intelligence. They're caused by people being deeply attached to beliefs that feel good or signal loyalty to their group, rather than trying to figure out what's actually true. If that fundamental orientation shifted, a lot of downstream problems would start solving themselves.

Curiosity is underrated as a force. When people are genuinely driven to understand things (instead of just being right or winning), they become harder to manipulate, more willing to update their views, and better at cooperating on hard problems. Tribalism does the opposite—it turns every issue into a team sport.

A secondary effect is that it would accelerate scientific and technological progress without needing to force it. The limiting factor for humanity right now isn't raw brainpower so much as how much of that brainpower gets wasted on signaling, status games, and defending comfortable narratives.

What would you change?
